title: The Star Coins
authors: After the Brothers Grimm, retold for Storytime Library
description: A kind girl gives away everything she has — and the night sky gives something wonderful back. A gentle bedtime retelling of the Grimm tale of the star money.

pages.alt: A girl in a plum-coloured dress stands alone on a grey hillside with a small loaf of bread.
pages.text: There was once a girl who had almost nothing at all — only the clothes she wore and one small loaf of bread. Still, she set out into the world with a hopeful heart.

pages.alt: The girl shares her loaf of bread with a hungry traveller on the path.
pages.text: On the road she met a hungry traveller. “Please, have my bread,” she said, and gave the whole loaf away. It felt light to give, and warm.

pages.alt: In a darkening pine forest, the girl gives her warm shawl to a cold child.
pages.text: In the woods she met a shivering child, so she gave away her warm shawl. A little farther on, another child had no cap — so she gave her cap away too.

pages.alt: The girl stands in a simple white shift under a rising moon.
pages.text: At last, in the deep quiet of the night, she gave away the very last thing she had to give. Now she owned nothing in the world — and the forest was dark all around.

pages.alt: Bright stars fall from the night sky and turn into gold coins around the smiling girl.
pages.text: Then the sky began to shimmer. One by one, the stars slipped loose and fell — tink! tink! tink! — landing all around her as bright gold coins, and she found herself wrapped in a brand-new gown, soft as starlight.

pages.alt: The girl walks toward a cozy cottage under the moon, coins glowing on the path.
pages.text: She gathered the star coins in her skirt, and from that night on she always had enough — enough to keep, and plenty to share. For a kind heart shines brighter than all the stars. The end.
